items.title: Register your business with the City of Aurora
items.description: Aurora runs a free business registration so the city can reach businesses in emergencies, and requires a business license for most businesses, renewed every two years.

items.title: Obtain Chicago business license
items.authority: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP)
items.description: Most Chicago businesses need a license for their activity and location, with zoning and inspection sign-off where applicable.

items.title: Provide Chicago Paid Leave and Paid Sick and Safe Leave
items.authority: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP)
items.description: Employers covered by the Chicago Paid Leave and Paid Sick and Safe Leave Ordinance must provide leave, post notice and keep records.

note: The city says non-home-based businesses register within 30 days of starting and some businesses need a license (calendar year); its pages could not be retrieved to confirm.
No general business license was found on the city's official pages; specific activities (tobacco, massage, hardship sales) are licensed.
The city's pages list sector-specific licenses (contractors, tobacco, tires, cannabis); a general license was not confirmed.
The city does not require a general business license for every business; specific business types are licensed, and licenses expire January 31 unless stated otherwise.
City Clerk licensing involves residency and background checks for some licenses; a general business license was not confirmed.
